what: Official implementation of RSIAgent — a training-free multi-agent framework (curriculum, actor, verifier) that recursively explores a new computer environment and consolidates verified experience into a memory that is frozen and reused at test time.
architecture: Three roles: Curriculum Agent (picks practice tasks from knowledge gaps, decides when practice stops), Actor Agent (code-as-policy execution; distills its own verified experience into memory), Verifier Agent (judges outcomes from environment evidence, isolated from the actor's private reasoning and memory).

Three runtime phases: Phase 1 BRS — parallel practice waves from a shared memory snapshot, consolidated serially per wave with budget checks at wave boundaries; Phase 2 DRS — sequential, progressively harder targeted practice, each verified experience committed to memory before the next; Phase 3 — frozen-memory task execution with the curriculum agent and memory updates disabled, followed by sealed official evaluation.

The host harness enforces isolation, records artifacts, commits memory only at valid boundaries (the wave barrier), and keeps benchmark setup and grading outside the learning loop; infra failures stay distinguishable from scored outcomes.
advantages: Wave-level parallelism with a real memory barrier: every Phase 1 branch starts from the identical pre-wave snapshot and no branch publishes memory until all branches pass verification, after which Actors distill serially in authored order — exploration scales horizontally without cross-branch memory races, and an incomplete or quarantined branch blocks the wave rather than silently poisoning memory.

Verifier isolation is an enforced boundary, not a prompt convention: the Verifier inspects a rollback-protected candidate with the Actor's private artifacts hidden and its guest-local mutations rolled back before the Actor resumes, returning PASS/FAIL/unresolved — and an infrastructure error is explicitly unscored, so a crash can never be laundered into a PASS or an official zero.

Weights-frozen RSI with a sealed exam fence (tools/exam_fence.py, tests/test_no_leakage.py): memory is the only persistent learning state, model parameters never change, and official evaluation runs after the Actor–Verifier loop with its output confined to the host — so a measured gain is attributable to memory/curriculum design rather than weight updates or benchmark contamination.
run: Python 3.12 + uv on a Linux host with Docker and /dev/kvm. Clone, `cp .env.example .env` and set OPENROUTER_API_KEY; paths default to this checkout and sibling dirs (override with RSIAGENT_ROOT / OSWORLD_ROOT / RSIAGENT_ENV_FILE). OSWorld: clone OSWorld-V2 at v2026.08.08 into ../OSWorld-V2, `uv sync --frozen`, `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r ../RSIAgent/requirements.txt`, activate that venv, then run the prep chain `tools/prepare_osworld_v2_release.py`, `tools/build_p2_corpus.py`, `tools/exam_fence.py build`, `tools/smoke_osworld.py --output results/smoke/osworld`, keeping the venv active for batches. ALE: `python3 scripts/setup_ale.py` (clones the pinned upstream; separate grader `.venv` and `.venv-ale-worker`), then `../agents-last-exam/.venv/bin/python run_ale.py prepare --os linux|windows` (~167 GiB Linux, ~157 GiB Windows per image). Batches: `python run_osworld.py --arm both --name run_01 --concurrency 1` (add --dry-run to print the plan); ALE `../agents-last-exam/.venv/bin/python run_ale.py run --arm both --output results/ale/run_01 --concurrency 1` then `... run_ale.py report`. Credential-free validation: `uv venv .venv --python 3.12`, `uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements-dev.txt`, `.venv/bin/python tools/check_rsi_release.py`.
note: The most complete open implementation of explore-verify-remember RSI at computer-use scale. Even without the VM rigs, read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (wave memory barrier, stopping rules, verifier isolation) and docs/PAPER.md (honest aggregation scope of the headline numbers).
_source_note: Read README (357 lines) via gh api, the full recursive tree, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/PAPER.md, docs/ALE.md, .env.example, and run_osworld.py / run_ale.py / scripts/setup_ale.py / tools/exam_fence.py / tools/check_rsi_release.py. All what/architecture/note claims check out against README plus ARCHITECTURE.md (role table, three-phase table, wave barrier in explore/phase1_wave.py, rollback-protected hidden-artifact verification, sealed evaluator as host artifact); what/architecture/note reproduced verbatim, no errors found. Three corrections to `run`: (1) ALE must be invoked with the separate grader interpreter ../agents-last-exam/.venv/bin/python — setup_ale.py refuses to install into root/.venv and the worker runs from .venv-ale-worker; (2) ALE base disks are ~167 GiB Linux / ~157 GiB Windows, not a flat 160-170 GiB; (3) OSWorld preparation is a four-step chain (build_p2_corpus.py and exam_fence.py build sit between prepare_osworld_v2_release.py and smoke_osworld.py), and the OSWorld-V2 venv must stay active for batch runs. README headline results (OSWorld 2.0 71.97 -> 78.98, ALE 83.75 -> 84.82 mean partial credit) deliberately not restated here; docs/PAPER.md flags them as manuscript-reported, baseline-retained for 41/82 and 48/67 tasks, and not a matched-protocol leaderboard result. High confidence.
